title: A Base and an Arm in One Frame Tree: World, Base, Mount, Tool, and How an Error in the Base Becomes an Error at the Hand

questions.question: What does the arm's inverse kinematics want its target in?
options: The world frame, so that every robot agrees
The frame of the tool, where the target is the origin
The frame of the mobile base
The arm's own base frame
questions.explanation: The arm's table of joints starts at its own base, so a target given in the world has to be taken through the inverse of that base's pose in the world first.

questions.question: A heading error of 1 degree moved a hand 0.9 m out by:
options: 5 mm, one for one
0.9 mm
157 mm
questions.explanation: A heading error swings everything out along the arm about the base's centre: one degree in radians, 0.01745, times 0.9 m is 15.7 mm.

questions.question: A position error of 5 mm in the base moved the hand:
options: 5 mm, one for one
15.7 mm, multiplied by the lever
Less than 5 mm, since the arm absorbs part of it
Nothing, because the arm's frame moves with the base
questions.explanation: Moving the base sideways moves everything on it by the same amount. Only a turn is multiplied by the distance out to the hand.

questions.question: A world point not turned into the arm's frame gives:
options: A small error that grows with the reach
A large steady error
An error only in height
A target the inverse kinematics refuses
questions.explanation: The two frames differ by wherever the base is and however it is turned, so the hand goes to a place that is wrong by that whole pose, the same every time.

questions.question: Why does a mobile manipulator need its heading to a fraction of a degree?
options: Its wheels slip more when it turns
Its camera is on the base and turns with it
The hand is far from the base's centre and the error is multiplied by that
The arm's joints are less accurate than the wheels
questions.explanation: A degree at 0.9 m is 15.7 mm at the hand, more than most grasps allow. A position error of the same size as the grasp tolerance is far easier to meet.

questions.question: What is assumed about the ground?
options: It is level, but its height changes from place to place
It may slope, and the mount's turn allows for that
It is flat: height, roll and pitch are zero
Nothing: the frames hold on any ground
questions.explanation: The base's pose here is x, y and a heading. A slope adds roll and pitch, which 33-05 has to deal with.
